children: By Shun Hatanaka / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer
Effissimo Capital Management, an investment fund founded by former members of the now-defunct Murakami Fund, is rapidly purchasing more shares of Japanese semiconductor-related stocks.
These are all mid-sized companies with significant market shares in their respective fields. Effissimo appears to be purchasing more shares if it determines that the stocks are undervalued.

According to Effissimo's report submitted to the Kanto Regional Finance Bureau on Monday, the company increased its outstanding shares of Japan Electronic Materials Corp., a manufacturer of semiconductor testing components, to 11.45%. On Tuesday, Effissimo reported an increase to 12.56%.

Japan Electronic Materials is a leading producer in Japan of "probe cards" used to test semiconductor performance. Driven by the expansion of the generative AI market, the company has increased its production volume. It forecasts about a 50% year-on-year increase in net income for the fiscal year ending March 2027.

Effissimo also submitted reports last Friday, showing that the firm held a 6.14% stake in Towa Corp., which boasts a world-leading market share in semiconductor sealing technology, and a 5.07% stake in Osaka Organic Chemical Industry Ltd., a global leader in materials used to form semiconductor circuits.

While Effissimo states in the reports that the purpose of holding these shares is "purely for investment," it also says it plans to increase its stake in each company by more than 5 percentage points within three months, depending on stock prices.

Following the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3, when the Democratic Party took control of Congress, semiconductor-related stocks in Japan have been notably weak due to concerns regarding AI regulations.
The three semiconductor-related companies have reported strong financial results.
"If their stock prices are deemed low relative to their earnings forecasts, (Effissimo) may increase its ownership stakes (in those companies)," an analyst said.
